title: Monster
subtitle: The choice to keep saving people

entry.breathQuote: I started it because people called it the greatest thriller ever drawn. I kept watching because it asked a question I'd been avoiding: what do I owe the people I've already hurt?

reflection.quote: Johan isn't the monster of the title. The monster is the idea that some people can be written off. Tenma spends the whole story refusing to write anyone off — that's the whole battle.
reflection.whatIKept: Compassion can be a decision, not a feeling. Grimmer learned to smile like a textbook and still chose to use it on other people. That stayed with me.
reflection.definingScene: Grimmer, after everything, whispering 'I am smiling.' A man who never felt a thing, deciding to be kind anyway — because it was right, not because it felt good.
reflection.whoItMadeMeThinkAbout: The small cruelties I excuse because they're small — and the people who became who they are because someone wrote them off.

thoughtCascade.thought: One life over another. He made the wrong choice for the right reasons.
The boy he saved grows up to be the thing he feared most.
Johan is terrifying because he's empty, not because he's cruel.
Grimmer says 'I am smiling' and I had to pause the episode.
I spent a week wondering which of my compromises feed something I don't want to name.

cinematicMoment.title: The mayor or the boy.
cinematicMoment.body: Tenma had a second — a real second — where his hand almost went to the famous man. Then he chose the boy. It's the same second everyone gets, and I keep asking myself what I would have done.

memoryCards.question: What stayed with me after the screen went dark?

cards.title: The Scalpel
cards.text: His instrument of salvation and, indirectly, of the wound. We are responsible for what we create, even accidentally.

cards.title: The Smile
cards.text: Grimmer's smile is a learned behavior — and he still chooses to point it outward. Kindness is a practice, not a mood.

cards.title: The Picture Book
cards.text: The nameless monster: a child who decides he has no name. What happens when identity is stolen before it's built.

altMemories.question: What quietly changed?
altMemories.heading: I stopped believing evil is a category.
altMemories.body: Johan stopped being a villain to me and became an answer to a question: what happens to a child who is never treated as a person? I started seeing cruelty as evidence of something, not proof of someone's nature.
altMemories.caption: Monsters are made — out of people.

altMemories.question: What did I admire?
altMemories.heading: Tenma never stops running.
altMemories.body: He made one mistake, then spent the whole story trying to undo it — knowing he can't. Responsibility isn't a feeling. It's a motion you keep making.
altMemories.caption: Guilt is a compass, not a prison.

pullQuote.text: I am smiling. I am smiling.

firstImpression.heading: A tense thriller
firstImpression.body: I expected a chase: genius detective hunts serial killer. The show delivered the opposite — a doctor chasing his own past.

whatShifted.heading: The question underneath
whatShifted.body: It stopped being about catching Johan and became about why he exists. Every monster in the story was made by the same machine.

whatStayed.heading: Radical compassion
whatStayed.body: Tenma's refusal to kill, even at the end, isn't weakness — it's the thesis. The only way out is refusing to write anyone off.

items.line: when I dehumanize someone for convenience.
to make compassion a practice rather than a mood.
the small cruelties I excuse because they're small.

characters.name: Kenzo Tenma
characters.mirror: He reflected my own relationship with my mistakes: the constant motion of trying to fix what can't be fixed — and refusing to stop anyway.

characters.name: Johan Liebert
characters.mirror: He made me uncomfortable because he's not a reason to give up on people. He's the reason you never start writing people off.

characters.name: Wolfgang Grimmer
characters.mirror: He had every reason to become a monster and chose to be the warmest person in the room. I keep him as a standard.

notes.text: The scariest moment isn't Johan. It's realizing how many people would do exactly what he asks.
Tenma runs from his past and spends the whole show running toward it. That's just what accountability looks like.

ideas.application: Identity is built in childhood, and every adult I influence is either giving someone a name or taking one away.
Treating people's worst acts as symptoms to understand, not verdicts to enforce. It doesn't excuse — it explains, and explanation is where change starts.

continueJourney.because: Because I keep meeting the question of what I owe the people I've already hurt — and I no longer believe the answer is nothing.

recommendations.title: Psycho-Pass
recommendations.reason: When the system itself decides who is a criminal.
